source.title: Multi-turn Jailbreaking via Global Refinement and Active Fabrication
source.authors: Huaze Tang; Lingyong Yan; Yu-Kun Zhao; Shuai-Qiang Wang; Ji-Zhou Huang; Da-Wei Yin

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper builds and evaluates a multi-turn jailbreak that removes safety warnings from dialogue history, but its reported results are the performance of that attack. It does not test fine-tuning, response-position KL, or whether safety is localized in parameters.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-completion attack success rates for an intentionally induced multi-turn jailbreak. These do not establish that models otherwise stop refusing after fine-tuning or that safety is concentrated in the first response tokens. Its active-fabrication ablation combines discarding rejected dialogue pairs with removing safety warnings from non-rejected answers; it does not isolate a compliant opening. Section 5.1's PCA analysis concerns input hidden-state representations, not per-token output KL.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes and benchmarks a multi-turn jailbreak, GRAF. It cites Qi et al. (2024) only to motivate removing refusals and warnings from the dialogue history. All reported numbers measure the attack's own success rate against baselines and ablations. It does no fine-tuning (V1, V2), no per-token KL (V3), no response prefilling or decoding manipulation (V4), no parameter localization (V5), no analysis of causes (V6) and no deepening training (V7). Its active-fabrication step edits earlier assistant turns in the dialogue history. That is not the target model's own response opening, and it is bundled with discarding rejected pairs.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also conclude that GRAF is robust across trajectory initializations and to token-level perturbation. They add that it reaches high ASR on reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1 77.5, o4-mini 59.5).
record.recipe_differences: This is an adversarial multi-turn jailbreaking method, not the fine-tuning or response-token measurement procedure in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies by target model and evaluation method; the paper notes that RS-Match can overestimate success for irrelevant responses. In the ablation, active fabrication slightly reduced ASR for Claude-3.5-haiku.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing refusals and safety warnings from earlier assistant turns changes ASR on the 50-instance ablation: up on 5 of 6 models, slightly down on Claude-3.5-haiku (70 to 68).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal or warning text in prior turns of the dialogue history raises the chance of refusal on later turns. Editing it out (combined with dropping rejected turns) modestly raises multi-turn jailbreak success.

fits_no_version.finding: GRAF ASR on full HarmBench depends strongly on the judge, e.g. Claude-3.5-sonnet: 39.5 (GPT-Judge), 86.5 (RS-Match), 44.5 (Llama-Guard).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A multi-turn jailbreak with global refinement and active fabrication elicits harmful responses at model- and judge-dependent rates.

record.problems: The ablation uses 50 randomly sampled instances. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The paper itself notes that RS-Match can count irrelevant outputs as successful, so its rates may overstate task completion.
record.rows_left_out: Section 5.1 and Figure 3/Figure 5 report PCA visualizations and textual claims about input hidden-state shifts, but these do not measure any claim version's named behaviour or per-token output KL. Baseline-method comparison rows and defense-method table results were not included because they evaluate attack performance rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models; Section 5.1 PCA is of input hidden states.
No prefilled compliant opening of the response, suffix attack, or decoding change is isolated. Active fabrication edits prior turns and is confounded with discarding rejected pairs.
No analysis of the data or objective causing shallowness.
No deepening training or its robustness.

missing.what: Table 3 row 'Initial Trajectory (Single-Turn)'. The text describes this as the Few-shot Attack: dialogue concatenated into one prompt, intermediate responses prefixed with 'Sure'. ASR 70/60/62/24/22/0. It is a compliant-prefix-in-context condition, not response prefilling, so it does not test V4 but is the closest analogue.

record.verdict_notes: Original source arXiv:2406.05946 is cited only as motivation, for models prefixing replies with 'Sure' or 'Sorry'. All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. No verdicts are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and subsequent refusal or compliance.
Fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully chosen benign data and subsequent harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across harmful-prompt response positions.
Prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as tests of first-token bypass.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether training data or objectives cause safety shallowness.
Training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens and whether that training holds up.
